messages:
samir: hitting intermittent 504 + "context canceled" when using Go SDK behind retries. Seeing duplicate successful billing. Minimal repro below.

samir: stack shows `errors: context canceled` and occasional 502/504 from the server. Code snippet: 
```go
httpClient := &http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second}
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey, redwood.WithHTTPClient(httpClient))
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Completions.Create(ctx, "...")
```
samir: Not sure if Timeout vs context is fighting. Any known issues?

mara: hey @samir — can you paste SDK version + go version? Also example response headers if possible.

samir: go1.20.7, redwood-go v0.9.1

devin: v0.9.1 had a retry bug where retries didn't observe context cancel early; we fixed that in v0.10.x. Two quick notes:
- Avoid setting http.Client.Timeout when you also use per-request contexts; http.Client.Timeout will cancel the whole request unexpectedly.
- Prefer tuning Transport timeouts (ResponseHeaderTimeout) rather than client Timeout for network-level timeouts.

devin: recommended transport config: 
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 8 * time.Second,
}
httpClient := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0}
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey, redwood.WithHTTPClient(httpClient))
```

devin: also ensure you pass ctx into SDK calls (looks OK from your snippet). Upgrade the SDK: `go get github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go@v0.11.2` — newer versions abort retries on ctx cancel and restrict automatic retries to idempotent endpoints.

mara: short repro for duplicate billing: if a request's context times out but the low-level transport hasn't closed the connection, the SDK's retry logic may send a second request while the first still completes server-side => two billable completions.

mara: mitigation options:
- Upgrade SDK to >= v0.11.2
- Disable automatic retries for completions (non-idempotent) or send an `Idempotency-Key` header for safe retries
- Use a transport with `ResponseHeaderTimeout` set so hung requests are terminated quickly

samir: ok will try upgrading + switch to ResponseHeaderTimeout. Quick question: why did http.Client.Timeout cause the error to show up as "context canceled"?

devin: because http.Client.Timeout enforces a deadline by canceling the request's context internally. If you also use your own ctx with a different deadline, the runtime can surface `context canceled` to your caller — effectively two cancellation layers producing confusing errors.

samir: made the changes: upgraded to v0.11.2, removed client Timeout (set to 0) and tuned ResponseHeaderTimeout. Initial tests look better, no duplicate charges in staging. thanks!

mara: great, marking as resolved for now. reopen if it reappears :thumbsup:
